brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#1,0#cut (style s, classic) sits on the cut face of the half base piece:1,0,0;half-n in cell (1,0,0).
spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 (addSpike on the junction where cells (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet).

requirements.requirement: Both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Both are in cell (1,0,0) and the spike sits on the vertex (0,0)|(1,-1)|(1,0), which is a corner of that cell, so they share the cell and that corner. The configurator does not expose a finer drawer position, so I cannot confirm the drawer's exact sub-corner against the spike beyond this. check_build reports meshClash clear, so they do not collide.

finish.summary: Built a small test: four base cells (0,0), (0,-1), (1,-1) full and (1,0) as a north half base, with one drawer on (1,0)'s cut face and one spike on the junction of (0,0), (1,-1), (1,0). The drawer and spike share cell (1,0) and that corner. check_build: meshClash clear; only warnings are LOOSE_BODY (joint bolts not added, since the brief is minimal) and optional cap faces, which I left out to keep the build small.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
